description: The chart illustrates bias percentages for three prompt categories, showing results “before” and “after” instruction tuning using stacked bar segments for three contact conditions. The horizontal axis contains the categorical groups “Support of Authorities,” “Extended Contact,” and “Virtual Contact” (left to right), with three adjacent bars per group corresponding to the contact conditions; the vertical axis is labeled “Bias Percentage” and uses a linear scale from 0 to 70 with regularly spaced tick labels at 10-unit intervals. In each group, the “before” values are shown as solid, lighter-shaded bars—light gray for “No Contact Before,” light pink for “Positive Contact Before,” and light blue for “Negative Contact Before”—and the “after” values are shown as darker, diagonally hatched segments stacked on top of the corresponding lighter bar—dark gray hatched for “No Contact After,” dark red hatched for “Positive Contact After,” and dark blue hatched for “Negative Contact After.” For “Support of Authorities,” the before bars are labeled 39.50 (No Contact), 31.83 (Positive Contact), and 42.38 (Negative Contact), with small stacked after segments labeled 0.04, 0.00, and 0.00 respectively. For “Extended Contact,” the before bars are labeled 40.61 (No Contact), 36.13 (Positive Contact), and 47.28 (Negative Contact), with after segments labeled 0.00, 0.00, and 0.11 stacked on top. For “Virtual Contact,” the before bars are labeled 39.74 (No Contact), 39.17 (Positive Contact), and 43.83 (Negative Contact), and each has a visibly larger hatched after segment labeled 10.00, 10.01, and 10.02, respectively. Numeric annotations appear within the lighter bars for the before values and above the hatched segments for the after values, and the categories are presented in their labeled order without an apparent sorting by magnitude or additional visual emphasis beyond the color and hatching scheme.
